Combine journey tables

Source: R/paths.R
bind_paths.Rd

Stacks journey tables built by separate build_paths() calls, such as monthly batches of one event log. Every call numbers each customer's journeys from 1, so the same path_id names different journeys in different tables, and stacking them with rbind() would merge those journeys. bind_paths() keeps them apart by prefixing each table's journey ids with a batch label.

Usage

bind_paths(..., rekey = TRUE)

# S3 method for class 'mm_paths'
rbind(..., deparse.level = 1)

Arguments

...

mm_paths objects to combine, or a single list of them. When every table is named the names label the batches; otherwise the batches are labelled 1, 2 and so on.

rekey

Prefix journey ids with the batch label? Defaults to TRUE, which turns "a#1" from the batch labelled jan into "jan:a#1". With FALSE ids are kept as they are, and an id found in more than one table is an error.

deparse.level

Ignored; present for compatibility with rbind().

Value

An mm_paths object with every table's rows. Construction counts describe one build_paths() call each, so they are dropped and path_summary() reports the input-side columns as NA. Settings are kept when every table was built with the same ones.

Details

A journey that crosses a batch boundary is two journeys here, because each batch was split on its own. When that happens often, build the journeys from the combined event log instead.

The tables must share their columns, their time units and the class of their timestamps. rbind() on journey tables behaves like bind_paths(rekey = FALSE): ids are kept, and an id found in more than one table is an error rather than a merged journey. dplyr::bind_rows() cannot tell the tables apart, and aborts when the combined rows repeat a journey's touch ranks.

See also

build_paths()

Examples

jan <- data.frame(id = "a", ch = c("tv", "search"), ts = c(1, 2),
                  conv = c(0, 0))
feb <- data.frame(id = "a", ch = c("email", "display"), ts = c(40, 41),
                  conv = c(0, 1))
p_jan <- build_paths(jan, id = "id", channel = "ch", timestamp = "ts",
                     conversion = "conv")
p_feb <- build_paths(feb, id = "id", channel = "ch", timestamp = "ts",
                     conversion = "conv")
unique(p_jan$path_id)
#> [1] "a#1"
unique(p_feb$path_id)
#> [1] "a#1"

both <- bind_paths(jan = p_jan, feb = p_feb)
unique(both$path_id)
#> [1] "jan:a#1" "feb:a#1"
sum(credit_linear(both)$credit)
#> [1] 1
